all_quick_tuner_timings.justification: The best result so far (iter 3) used 10 ms latency, 1 ms granularity, full CPU perf, and POLL idle suppression. I’m now pushing the knobs to a new but still safe corner: slightly lower latency (5 ms), even shorter granularity (0.5 ms), higher busy-poll to cut Rx wake-up delay, and C1E instead of POLL to see if we can preserve the 1 ms p99 without the energy hit of POLL. Keeping 80-100 % CPU perf avoids clock ramp-up stalls. This probes an adjacent region without abandoning the promising ultra-low-latency settings.

reasoning.justification: Exploring latency reduction by halving scheduler/wakeup latencies while restricting deep C-states and locking CPU performance to maximum. This tests the hypothesis that scheduler responsiveness is the primary bottleneck for p99 latency.

all_quick_tuner_timings.justification: The single best measurement so far (1.09) came from POLL + highest CPU lock, but we only sampled two nearby points.  Instead of chasing the 1.1-class configs again, I now probe a slightly wider-granularity, longer-latency window (7 ms / 3 ms) that still keeps the CPU at full throttle and disables C-states.  This gives the Actor fresh data on whether the 8 ms setting in iter 11 was an outlier peak or a repeatable sweet spot, while staying in safe territory.
